subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should core `gog gmail attachment` own in-process PDF text extraction for untrusted email attachments, or should this PR be narrowed to bounded inline bytes until extraction can be isolated?
rationale: Tests cannot settle whether an incomplete PDF parser belongs inside the CLI/MCP trust boundary or what resource limits maintainers are willing to support.

options.title: Narrow to inline bytes
options.body: Land `--inline` after output and proof fixes, and defer `--text` until a bounded extraction design is available.

options.title: Isolate text extraction
options.body: Keep `--text` but run PDF parsing with enforceable timeout and memory or process boundaries plus malicious-input tests.

options.title: Accept in-process parsing
options.body: Ship the current parser boundary and explicitly own the availability risk for crafted or pathological PDFs.

recommendation.title: Narrow to inline bytes
recommendation.body: Land `--inline` after output and proof fixes, and defer `--text` until a bounded extraction design is available.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release integration history makes this the strongest available owner for deciding the permanent CLI and dependency boundary.
